flashcard_questions.q: (Higher) What causes gas pressure inside a container?
flashcard_questions.a: Gas particles colliding with the walls of the container.

flashcard_questions.q: (Higher) What is the SI unit of pressure?
flashcard_questions.a: The pascal, equal to one newton per square metre.

flashcard_questions.q: (Higher) How many pascals are in one kilopascal?
(Higher) Why does heating a sealed container of gas raise the pressure?
flashcard_questions.a: Particles move faster and hit the walls more often and harder.

flashcard_questions.q: (Higher) What equation is used for Boyle's law calculations?
(Higher) Why does increasing the volume of a gas lower its pressure?
flashcard_questions.a: Particles travel further before hitting the walls, so collisions are less frequent.

flashcard_questions.q: (Higher) p = ____ × ____ × ____, the pressure in a column of liquid.
(Higher) Why does pressure in a liquid increase with depth?
flashcard_questions.a: There is a greater weight of liquid in the column above.

flashcard_questions.q: (Higher) How does the density of a liquid affect pressure at a given depth?
flashcard_questions.a: A denser liquid gives a higher pressure at the same depth.

flashcard_questions.q: (Higher) What is atmospheric pressure at sea level?
(Higher) Why does atmospheric pressure fall as altitude increases?
flashcard_questions.a: There is a shorter column of air above, so less weight presses down.

flashcard_questions.q: (Higher) What causes the upthrust on an object in a fluid?
flashcard_questions.a: The pressure on its bottom face is greater than on its top face.

flashcard_questions.q: (Higher) When does an object float in a fluid?
flashcard_questions.a: When the upthrust equals its weight.

flashcard_questions.q: (Higher) When does an object sink in a fluid?
flashcard_questions.a: When its weight is greater than the upthrust.

flashcard_questions.q: (Higher) Why does a steel ship float even though steel is dense?
flashcard_questions.a: Its hull displaces a large volume of water, giving enough upthrust.

notes: 15 cards, every one prefixed '(Higher)' because the whole lesson body sits inside a higher-only block. Mix is 1 cloze on the p = hρg equation, 1 equation-recall card for Boyle's law, 2 value-and-unit cards (pascal, kilopascal, atmospheric pressure at sea level), 6 'why' particle-model explanation cards, 2 float/sink condition cards with opposite answers, 1 real-world application. Dropped all three worked calculations as practice-question material; no single-word answers were used except the numeric 1000, because the '(Higher)' prefix would otherwise fail the validator's single-word question pattern.
